World rule: Add explicit build-translation rules for player builds (home, cafe, skyscraper, car, dog), which currently ignore the bible. No chimneys (smoke-holes only). No rectangular cut-stone, plaster or plank walls. No doors with lintels, hanging signs or plaques. No tables or stools; seating is logs and stones. Domes, finials, pagoda eaves and regular storeys are banned. Homes are round or oval hide, branch-and-daub or mammoth-bone huts. The skyscraper is a stacked boulder or cliff terrace with log ladders and cave mouths. The car is a hauled sledge or travois with no seat, steering bar, headlights or painted panels. The dog is wolf-like with no saddle or harness.
World rule: Add to avoid: masonry or brick chimneys, painted sign boards on buildings, painted coloured lumber, headlamps and cushions. Smoke holes with protruding poles only.
elements.fix: Preserve the dwelling footprint and capacity, but rebuild it as an irregular pole-and-hide shelter with overlapping roof skins, visible ties and a simple smoke opening instead of a chimney stack. Replace the tiled approach with trampled earth and a rough threshold stone, and use sparse asymmetric wild growth rather than matched shrubs. / Remove the chimney entirely and put a dark smoke-hole at the roof apex with 2–3 pole tips poking out. Rebuild the house as a round or oval hut about 6 m across: a low ring of piled stones or mud-daub (0.5 m) with an irregular conical roof of hide and branch panels (6–8 tilted slabs in varied tans and browns), or a mammoth-bone hut with tusk arches over the doorway. The doorway should be an open hide flap held by two crooked poles, no lintel. Swap the plaque for an ochre handprint on a hide flap. Keep the outdoor fire and log seats. / Remove the chimney. Instead, have 5–6 roof poles cross and poke 0.6 m out of the apex around a smoke hole. Make the walls a round wattle-and-daub drum (cylinder) in mud tones, or have hides lean right to the ground. Break the cone roof into 2–3 tiers or patchwork hide panels in different tans. Make the doorway a larger dark hide-flap opening (1.2 × 1.8 m) with a pale pulled-back flap, and put a firepit and drying rack outside.
